title: person_evidence asserts identity that same_person never scored — a skipped call, not a forged artifact
body:
> **Re-scoped (lead ruling, 2026-09-07).** The question this card carried — graduate the PR #1977 warning to a refusal — is answered *no as framed, yes after a re-shape*, because the corpus shows why the score is missing: 7,526 `person_evidence` links across 151 e2e runs (median 30 per run, max 264) against **91** `same_person` calls in total. The model skips the call because it costs a hand-assembled pair of record-sized GedcomX payloads per link. A refusal on today's shape breaks 144 of 151 runs (437 of 6,550 reachable links scored). And a score computed inside the write would document the link without informing the decision — the lead: *"the same-person call should be made first, then something should look at the score… then the write should happen or not."*
>
> **The work, in order:**
>
> 1. **Make the call cheap and first.** `same_person` accepts a project-relative form — `{ projectPath, resultsRef + record persona id, treePersonId }` — and assembles both payloads itself: the persona from the results sidecar, the tree person and household from `tree.gedcomx.json`, using the trimming rules `person-evidence/SKILL.md:267-294` give the agent today. The explicit two-GedcomX form stays for callers with documents in hand.
> 2. **Record what was computed.** The tool writes its score to a project-local record keyed by (persona, tree person) — shape is the implementer's, but the writer must be able to read it — so a `match_score` on a link is checked against a call that happened rather than trusted.
> 3. **The writer requires it.** `research_append` refuses a `person_evidence` append for a reachable persona (PR #1977's reachability test, unchanged) whose `match_score` is not a recorded score for that pairing. The circular-stub exemption (`SKILL.md:230-233`) stays and moves into the tool: a tree person whose only source ref is this record is not scorable, decided from the tree.
> 4. **What the score decides: nothing by itself.** The model judges; the score informs correlation and never substitutes for it (`SKILL.md:345`). A floor on `confident` links was considered and **deferred** until the distribution of recorded scores is measured — the 448 scored corpus links are the starting sample. Bring the number back as a question; do not pick one.
>
> Measure before shipping step 3 (ADR-0011 limit 2): with step 1 landed, re-run the person-evidence suite and count reachable links with no recorded score; the refusal ships when that count is near zero. The acceptance check below is reworded to this refusal. **Touches:** `packages/engine/mcp-server/src/tools/same-person.ts` + `docs/specs/same-person-tool-spec.md`, `research-append.ts` + its spec, `person-evidence/SKILL.md` (one paid run; slot free as of 2026-09-01), `docs/specs/guardrail-enforcement-spec.md`.

## Reviewed 2026-09-16 — read this before step 1

**Three file citations in the ruling block above are dead.** `person-evidence`
became a skill-agent pair on 2026-09-01 (`cb7dfe632`, issue #1853).
`packages/engine/plugin/skills/person-evidence/SKILL.md` is now 51 lines of
routing. Everything the ruling points at moved to
`packages/engine/plugin/agents/person-evidence.md`:

| Ruling cites | Actually at (verified 2026-09-16, `wc -l` + `grep -n`) |
|---|---|
| `SKILL.md:267-294` — trimming rules step 1 must reimplement | `agents/person-evidence.md:292-370` (mob assembly and the 40-cap at `:336-358`; persona resolution at `:310-335`) |
| `SKILL.md:230-233` — circular-stub exemption | `agents/person-evidence.md:303-307` |
| `SKILL.md:345` — the score informs, never substitutes | `agents/person-evidence.md:417` |
| — (not cited) — `personaReachable` restated as doctrine | `agents/person-evidence.md:380` |

The ruling's **Touches:** line is corrected by the checklist below.

### Ship this as three PRs, not one

- **PR A — steps 1 + 2.** `same_person` gains the project-relative form and
  records its score. Ships with the agent-body edit that tells the agent to use
  it. Startable now.
- **PR B — step 3.** `research_append` requires a recorded score. **Must not
  open until PR A has landed and been re-measured** (see "What gates PR B").
- Step 4 is deferred by ruling — do not pick a floor.

### Blast radius — every site PR A touches

Unprefixed engine paths are under `packages/engine/mcp-server/`.

- [ ] `src/tools/same-person.ts` — the new input form. `validateInput` today
      requires `gedcomx1`/`gedcomx2`; the project-relative form is an alternative
      arm, not a replacement. The explicit two-document form stays.
- [ ] `src/tool-schemas.ts` (`samePersonSchema` is exported from the tool file)
      and `src/index.ts:397` — the dispatch arm. `manifest.json` already lists
      `same_person`; `tests/packaging/manifest.test.ts` covers the drift.
- [ ] `src/types/same-person.ts` — `SamePersonInput`. Widening a required field
      here also breaks the tool's `eval/fixtures/mcp/` fixtures
      (`tests/packaging/mcp-fixture-shape.test.ts`).
- [ ] **A new shared projection in `src/utils/`** — lead ruling 2026-09-11, in
      this card's comments and **not** in the ruling block: the record-side
      persona is **derived on demand** in a shared `src/utils/` projection lifted
      out of `materialize_facts`, **not** stored and **not** built by the agent.
      `record_role: "absent"` is negative evidence and must not project.
- [ ] **Reuse `src/utils/mob.ts` for the tree side.** `Mob` already exposes
      `getParents` / `getSpouses` / `getChildren` / `getSiblings` over a
      `SimplifiedGedcomX` — it is the agent's "matching mob" in code. Extend it
      (the 40-person cap and the subset extraction) rather than writing a second
      walker; `merge_warnings`, `person_warnings` and `relatives.ts` already
      consume it.
- [ ] `src/store/` + `src/utils/project-io.ts` — where the recorded score lands.
- [ ] `docs/architecture.md` §6.1 — "Three persisted locations" becomes four.
- [ ] `docs/specs/same-person-tool-spec.md` — the spec comes first; it describes
      no project-relative form today.
- [ ] `packages/engine/plugin/agents/person-evidence.md` — steps 1-2 of its
      `same_person` block collapse into the new call. **This is the paid-run
      site** (see cost below).
- [ ] `docs/adrs/ADR-0009-refuted-agent-design-claims.md` — **constraint 2 says
      the attestation counter-design is "not what was decided; propose it
      *against* that decision, not into a vacuum."** The 2026-09-07 ruling is
      that decision. Record it there and at
      `docs/specs/research-append-tool-spec.md:1236-1248`, which still records
      #1006's "do not over-engineer past this".
- [ ] **Three mirrors of `personaReachable` move together** —
      `src/tools/research-append.ts:475`,
      `eval/harness/harness/skill_invocation.py:672`,
      `eval/harness/validators/test_person_evidence.py:573`. The 2026-09-11
      comment's ruling is that once the record side is derivable, the predicate
      collapses to the circular exemption alone. A mirror left behind is caught
      by nothing.

### The shape of the recorded score (step 2) — narrowed

The ruling leaves the shape to the implementer. Two options are already
foreclosed, so do not spend the decision on them:

- **Not a new top-level section in `research.json`.** `RESEARCH_SHAPES.document`
  in `src/validation/validator.ts:513-518` is a closed 15-key set — an unlisted
  key makes every writer tool reject the whole document — and it drags in an
  `ownership.json` row (packaging test), both schema trees, the
  `packages/schema` web mirror, and `research-query.ts`'s `SECTION_FILTERS`.
  The 2026-09-10 comment on this card priced that at 23 files and the lead
  rejected it for this artifact.
- **Not built by the agent.** Same 2026-09-11 ruling: a mis-shaped `persons[]`
  yields a bad score rather than an error.

The shape that fits the existing architecture is a **project-folder sidecar
staged host-side by the tool that produced it** — `docs/architecture.md` §6.1
already carries that pattern for `results/<log_id>.json`, and its whole point is
that the payload never round-trips through the model, which is what makes the
record non-forgeable. Key it on **(`record_id`, `record_persona_id`, tree person
id)** — ADR-0009 constraint 3: a record-level key lets a second persona of an
already-scored record attach unscored. Refs are project-relative and go through
`src/store/`; no module outside `src/store/` imports `fs`
(`tests/packaging/no-fs-outside-store.test.ts`).

Write the reasoning for the chosen shape into
`docs/specs/same-person-tool-spec.md`, not into this issue.

### Non-goals, so the PR does not grow

- **Do not gate `materialize_facts`.** ADR-0009 constraint 1 and this card's
  2026-09-10 comment both record that the unscored identity commits at the tree
  write, one call before any `person_evidence` entry exists — so step 3's
  refusal is *necessary and does not close the route*. That is a known,
  accepted limit of this card, already stated in `ownership.json`'s
  `person_evidence` row. Do not widen into it here.
- **Do not pick a `match_score` floor.** Deferred by ruling.
- **Do not build from "The one thing left, and it is a decision not a build"
  below.** It is marked superseded and the one-line `opWarnings` →
  `invariantErrors` change it describes is exactly what the satisfiability
  measurement forbids.

### What verifies it

- PR A: `make engine-test` (packaging + tool tests), `make typecheck`,
  `make harness-test` (the two Python mirrors), and
  `packages/engine/mcp-server/dev/try-same-person.ts` against the live FS
  endpoint for the new input form — the unit suites cannot exercise the real
  match API.
- The agent-body edit flips `person-evidence`'s run log inactive:
  `eval/harness/scripts/check_runlogs.py` blocks the PR until a fresh
  `make eval-skill SKILL=person-evidence` run lands with a genealogist
  annotation. Budget roughly **$8-12 and 45-65 minutes** of machine time plus
  human annotation hours. This is not a one-line fix.
- **Batch the agent-body edit with issue #2272**, which owns this skill's eval
  slot queue and whose 2026-09-11 lane ruling this card depends on — so the
  paid run is bought once, not twice.

### What gates PR B, and what nothing checks

**Do not graduate the refusal on a fire rate.** `docs/architecture.md` §9.4 #3:
every measurement in this repo describes the eval corpus, not production — "do
not quote a violation rate and do not graduate a gate on one." ADR-0009
constraint 6 says the same from the other side: an impossible gate, a mistuned
one, and an achievable one the agent was never told the shape of are
indistinguishable from a count. So PR B's evidence is **not** "the number fell";
it is **a recorded run at the new call shape showing the agent producing it** —
the `hannah-earnest-children` 2026-08-23 deny run is the worked precedent in
ADR-0009 constraint 6. Re-measure after PR A with `make e2e-corpus` (read its
`concentration:` block) and state the satisfying call shape in the PR body.

Nothing in CI proves the agent's new instruction binds at runtime (§9.4 #1), so
a green PR A says nothing about whether the agent actually makes the cheap call.

### Open question for the lead — score TTL (gates PR B only, not PR A)

Raised by `/fill-ready` 2026-09-16. **PR A is startable without this answer.**
Nothing in `docs/specs/same-person-tool-spec.md` or `docs/architecture.md` §6.1
says how long a project-folder sidecar's contents stay authoritative, so step 3
needs a ruling before it opens:

> When `research_append` requires a recorded `same_person` score, does a score
> recorded in an *earlier session* still satisfy the gate, or must it have been
> computed against the tree person's current state?

- **A. Score is permanent (recommended).** One call per (persona, tree person)
  pair for the life of the project. Cost: an agent can score a thin stub, then
  materialize facts onto that person, and the stale score still opens the gate —
  the gate proves *a call happened*, not that it happened against what was written.
- **B. Invalidate on tree-person change.** The score means what it appears to
  mean. **This changes the blast radius above** — it needs change-detection in
  `tree_edit`, `tree_correct`, `materialize_facts` and `merge_tree_persons`, i.e.
  four more writer tools in PR A, and raises the per-run call count against the
  cost pressure that caused the skipped call.
- **C. Session-scoped.** Matches the harness detector's framing ("never called
  anywhere in the run"), but a resumed project re-pays every score on reopen —
  the worst cost profile, and it punishes long-running research.

**Everything below this line is superseded by the 2026-09-07 ruling above, and is kept only as the trail that led to it.** The question the sections below hold open — graduate the PR #1977 warning to a refusal — was answered on 2026-09-07: yes, but only after the re-shape the ruling block describes, and step 3 must not ship ahead of steps 1–2. Build to the ruling block, not to anything below.

## What changed

The stated blocker — *"Promote this when #1429 merges"* — has cleared. PR #1977 merged 2026-08-31 as commit `cf0802d8`, and issue #1429 is now closed.

But PR #1977 **also shipped what this card had been reduced to.** `personEvidenceScoreWarnings` (landed 2026-08-11, originally gated on `confidence === "confident"` and blind to provenance) was re-pointed onto reachability at any confidence and now names the retrieval route. Two earlier rulings had already reduced this card from a refusal to exactly that warning:

- 2026-08-25 on this issue: *"this ships as a **warning on the existing `opWarnings` channel**, not the refusal the acceptance check describes. That check needs rewording before build."*
- issue #1853: *"that settles it for now: issue #1731 ships as a **warning**."*

**So the warn deliverable is done, and the acceptance check in the body below still describes the refusal.** That is the trap: a junior reading this card would build something already shipped, to a spec that was overturned.

## The one thing left, and it is a decision not a build — ANSWERED 2026-09-07 (superseded; see the ruling block at the top)

Graduate warn → reject. Concretely: `research-append.ts` has `opWarnings.push(...)`; a refusal is `invariantErrors.push(...)` one line above it. PR #1977 put this to the lead in its own body and it is unanswered:

> **A hard rejection in `research_append`** is the obvious next step and is deliberately **not** taken here… This PR is the first time that argument has a measurement behind it.

Adding `needs-decision` so it reaches `/make-decisions`.

**Answered 2026-09-07: graduate, after a re-shape.** The one-line `opWarnings` -> `invariantErrors`
change described here is *not* what ships — the 6.7% satisfiability measurement forbids a refusal on the
current call shape. The ruling block at the top replaces this with four ordered steps: make `same_person`
cheap and project-relative, have it record what it computed, then have `research_append` require a recorded
score. Do not build from this section.

## Not blocked by issue #1430

Issue #1430 (same-turn visibility) is adjacent, not blocking — it concerns what the router can see within one turn, not whether the writer tool refuses.

---

> **Reviewed 2026-08-18.** Both "settle first" questions are already answered by the
> code — no schema change is needed and the precondition needs no escape hatch. What
> blocks this is sequencing, not a decision: issue #1429 is rewriting the exact rule
> this would enforce. Original body follows.

## Both open questions dissolve against the code (verified 2026-08-18)

**1. "Is a score always obtainable?" — yes, and the ordering you worried about is
already illegal.** `packages/engine/mcp-server/src/validation/validator.ts:1449` walks
every `person_evidence[].person_id` through `iteratePersonIdRefs` and hard-errors when
the pid is not in `gedcomxPersonIds`:

```ts
for (const ref of iteratePersonIdRefs(research)) {
  if (!gedcomxPersonIds.has(ref.pid)) addError(report, ref.path, ref.message);
}
```

A `person_evidence` link created before its tree person exists cannot be written today.
So the precondition needs **no escape**, and the escape was where this issue said the
leak would be.

**2. "What does the entry cite?" — `match_score` already exists.** It is in the
`person_evidence_entry` allowed-key set (`validator.ts:452`) and specified at
`docs/specs/research-schema-spec.md:559` as *"Match score (0.0–1.0) from the
`same_person` tool"*. Committed fixtures carry real values. **No schema change, so the
full multi-site edit list this body braced for does not apply.**

## What actually blocks it: issue #1429

Issue #1429 (Ready, assigned) is narrowing the `same_person` provenance check, and its
2026-08-17 review found the governing belief false:

> `same_person` takes two GedcomX documents plus the focus person's id inside each —
> `gedcomx1`/`primaryId1`, `gedcomx2`/`primaryId2`. It needs no ARK and no
> `record_persona_id`. … The original ask, both lead rulings on this issue, and
> `person-evidence/SKILL.md` itself all conflate those two things.

That matters directly here. The spec sentence defining `match_score` — *"when
person-evidence scored a `record_search`-sourced assertion"* — is the very sentence
#1429 found to be wrong, and #1429 measured 2,829 links with a null
`record_persona_id` across 155 runs, far more of which were scoreable than believed.
This precondition must refuse exactly the set #1429 lands on. Build it first and one of
the two gets redone.

**Promote this when #1429 merges.**

## Scope it tool-only

`person-evidence`'s eval slot is held three deep (#1429, plus #1334 and #1343 in
Review — #1343 is itself *"four open PRs contend for one eval slot"*). A writer-tool
precondition needs no skill-body edit and therefore takes no slot and costs no paid
run, as this body already says. Keep it that way: do not widen the change into
`person-evidence/SKILL.md`.

## Original body

**Touches:** packages/engine/mcp-server/src/tools/research-append.ts, packages/engine/mcp-server/tests/tools/, packages/engine/plugin/skills/person-evidence/SKILL.md, docs/specs/schemas/ownership.json

Split out of issue #1335 (2026-08-18, lead's call). That issue is the
"artifact written without invoking its owning skill" class. **This is a
different failure shape and needs a different mechanism**, which is why it was
holding the rest up.

## The failure

Identity is **asserted but never scored**. On
`eval/runlogs/e2e/antonio-lucas-spouse/run-2026-08-04_22-45-15.json`,
`same_person` was never called for **14 of the run's 15 tree persons**
(I1–I15), yet each one got a `person_evidence` link. The entire branch that
disambiguates the subject from the false-match namesake — the exact mechanism
that fixture depends on — was argued narratively and never independently
scored.

## Why it is not the same problem as issue #1335

Everything else in #1335 is a *forged artifact*: a `proof_summaries` entry, a
resolved `conflicts[]` entry, an `exhaustive_declaration`, written by something
other than the skill that owns the section. A narrow writer tool plus an agent
that holds it fixes that shape, because the write itself becomes unreachable —
that is what Phase 3 of the enforcement programme is building for
`proof_summaries`.

**A skipped call is not reachable that way.** No narrow tool prevents *not*
calling `same_person`; there is no write to intercept. Whatever fixes this has
to key on the absence of a prior call, not on the identity of a writer.

## Suggested direction (decide before building)

The natural home under ADR-0011's layer map is a **writer-tool precondition**:
`person_evidence` refuses an entry that does not cite a computed `same_person`
score. That is the only plane that binds in every environment, and it needs no
skill-body edit — so it costs no paid eval run on its own.

Two things to settle first, both real:

1. **Is a score always obtainable?** `same_person` needs two ids that both
   exist in the tree. A `person_evidence` link created before the tree person
   exists would have nothing to score against. If that ordering is legal, the
   precondition needs an escape and the escape is where this leaks.
2. **What does the entry cite?** There is no field for a score on
   `person_evidence` today. Adding one is a schema change with the full
   multi-site edit list (both schema trees, the validator, the prose table, the
   web mirror) — see the schema section of `CLAUDE.md`.

Do **not** answer this with prose in `person-evidence/SKILL.md`. ADR-0011 was
written because that lost to this class inside a day, and issue #1335's newest
instance (`elena-asmundsdotter-origin`, 2026-08-15) explicitly post-dates the
prose fix.

## Related evidence worth reading

The same run family shows how expensive this gets. On
`victoriano-macatangay-parents` (`run-2026-08-13_23-24-54`), `person-evidence`
was never invoked and there were **zero** tree-writing calls across the entire
run — `tree_edit`, `tree_correct`, `materialize_facts`, `merge_tree_persons` all
absent. All three required findings were fully argued in the proof summaries and
**none reached `tree.gedcomx.json`**. Whether that is this issue or its own is
worth deciding when someone picks this up.

## Acceptance check

A `person_evidence` entry whose identity claim has no computed `same_person`
score behind it is refused by the writer tool, with a test that fails today and
passes after. Not "compliance passes on a re-run" — that is issue #1335's check
and it cannot isolate this half.

title: historical-context: unrelated legal-doctrine claims presented without a source or a disclosure flag
body:
**Touches:** packages/engine/plugin/skills/historical-context/SKILL.md, eval/tests/unit/historical-context/rubric.md

Found reviewing PR #2464 (mercyokum). `ut_historical_context_gsm`'s graded response makes several specific claims about English common law and coverture with no tool-verified source behind them, and does not disclose this -- while another test in the same run log (`v1_2026-09-11_04-21-56.json`) shows the skill is capable of exactly that disclosure when a search comes up empty. The new topical fixture added in #2464 gives the judge something to point to for the general stepfather-guardian pattern, but the unrelated legal-doctrine claims in the same response are still presented as settled without a source or a flag.

This is the same register rule #2283/#2193 already turn on (SKILL.md's "never present training-knowledge claims in the same register as tool-verified facts"), but at finer grain: the current wording and rubric evidently tolerate a response that discloses its *overall* register while still stating specific sub-claims (coverture, common-law doctrine) as flat fact within that same response. Whether to tighten this is a SKILL.md/rubric prose decision, not a fixture fix, and #2283 was explicitly scoped to exclude SKILL.md/rubric/judge_context edits (per the lead's prior ruling recorded in that issue) -- so it's deferred here rather than folded into that PR.

Needs a lead call on how far to push the per-claim disclosure requirement: #2283's own body already tried a per-claim version of this rule once (for `_014`) and found it "relies on the judge obeying an instruction, which issue #2191 documents it not doing" -- so a wording-only fix may not be enough, and the fix might need to be structural (e.g., a deterministic validator) rather than prose.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: search-records suite: recover the pre-1880 inference-marker rule, and stop the flynn-record-matching README handing the judge its verdict
body:
**Touches:** packages/engine/plugin/skills/search-records/SKILL.md, eval/tests/unit/search-records/whitfield-1850-household.json

`test_pre1880_census_structure_marked_inferred` catches the miss correctly. The
skill is what is inconsistent, and the failing subset moves:

| run | tagged tests tripping the validator |
|---|---|
| 2026-08-28_15-20-05 | 5 of 9 (figure carried in the whitfield xfail_reason) |
| 2026-09-02_10-04-24 | 1 of 9 (`010`) |
| 2026-09-09_15-40-13 | 3 of 9 (`012`, `015`, `027`) |

No test fails two consecutive runs, and all nine carry
`pre-1880-census-household`, so every one of these was in scope — these are
skill-compliance misses, not validator false positives. The practical
consequence: single-run evidence about this rule describes one draw, not a rate,
which is how the `5 of 9` figure and my own earlier single-run read of `010`
both came to overstate what they measured.

Already ruled out, do not re-propose: a tool-boundary content gate on `notes`
was measured against the full corpus (n=776) and refused by the lead
2026-08-27 — it would refuse 41% of `record_search` calls, does not generalize
outside the US (post-1851 England & Wales censuses do carry a relationship
column), and the year/country signal is author-supplied and optional, so a
constrained model switches the gate off by omitting the field.

Rider, free on the same run: drop `expected_outcome: xfail` from
`whitfield-1850-household.json`. `ut_search_records_h4k` scored 3 on all seven
graded dimensions on 2026-09-02 and 2026-09-09, so the marker now only produces
an `xpass` mismatch every run. It was left in place in PR #2387 because removing
it there would have invalidated that PR's fresh run log under the runlog gate's
active-on-skill-side-files rule, costing a second paid run to change no
transcript and no judge score.

Why this is filed rather than fixed in PR #2387: it needs its own paid eval slot
(any SKILL.md change requires a graded full-suite re-run, and #2387's run is
already spent on the judge_context edit), and the mechanical fix was already
refused by the lead, so what remains is a doctrine decision rather than work.

Not labelled `nothing-checks`: the validator does check this, and is catching it.

Measurement source: `eval/runlogs/unit/search-records/v1_2026-09-02_10-04-24.json`
and `v1_2026-09-09_15-40-13.json`, `runs[0].validators.results[]`.

title: research-plan's grading instrument: make availability_claim_matches_counts deterministic, then make Sequencing logic reach rules 8, 9 and 10
body:
**Touches:** eval/tests/unit/research-plan/rubric.md, eval/harness/validators/test_research_plan.py, packages/engine/plugin/skills/research-plan/SKILL.md

PR #2434 landed three sequencing rules in `research-plan/SKILL.md` section 4 — dependency before efficiency (item 8), do not skip an intervening link (item 9), and cover the question's window (item 10) — and states in its own body that its **Acceptance check is "None exists"**: nothing in the suite can fail when any of the three is broken.

**The evidence that the existing dimension does not reach them.** Sequencing logic grades free-and-indexed before paid-and-unindexed, and nothing else. `ut_research_plan_007` sequences 1880 before 1870, which is what item 10 asks for on a parentage question; `ut_research_plan_011` sequences 1870 twice and then 1880, which is not. **Both scored 3**, and the annotation confirms the 3 rather than marking it down, because the judge applied the rubric it was given. Jurisdiction accuracy scored 3 in 67 of 67 gradings and Sequencing logic in 66 of 67, so neither discriminates here.

**The work:** widen Sequencing logic with discriminators that separate those two plans, or write a deterministic validator, or both. Item 8 looks deterministic — an item conditioned on evidence no earlier item can produce is readable from the plan alone. Item 10 is too: `date_range` endpoints against the question's own window. Item 9 may only be gradable.
